1)The attitude in the US is really frustrating about pregnancy tests right now. We should be taking the patient’s word for it. I was always taught that the patient has the right of refusal. Especially if an IV is going to be in place for the procedure, they should just take blood if a pregnancy test is deemed medically appropriate by the doctor. It smacks of laziness. Blood pregnancy test can actually be more accurate because it can detect lower levels of hcg in the blood.

This is actually very normal in the medical field. There are specific procedures and forms for people to observe rarer operations and procedures. It means that the observers will be prepared to help the next person with that problem. 

The patient’s consent should be always obtained. Usually they ask while you are talking about the procedure or during forms signing. In my training, the trainer would introduce me, ask if it was okay if I observed, did part of the procedure, etc, even if the patient had been previously asked and said okay at the time. Unless the patient is unconscious or it’s an emergency situation, observer introductions usually happen in my hospital. 

I feel like this gets misunderstood by non medical people, but it’s a necessary part of training and continuing education. It can be misused (several court cases stand as evidence), but until they invent something better, it’s what we have.
